pumac-2012-finals-a-01.prompt: Let $p$ be a prime number greater than $5$. Prove that there exists a positive integer $n$ such that $p$ divides $20^n+15^n-12^n$.
pumac-2012-finals-a-01.answer: $n=p-3$ works: since $\frac1{20^2}+\frac1{15^2}=\frac1{12^2}$, Fermat's little theorem gives $p\mid 20^{p-3}+15^{p-3}-12^{p-3}$.

pumac-2012-finals-a-02.prompt: Let $a,b,c$ be real numbers such that $a+b+c=abc$. Prove that $$\frac1{a^2+1}+\frac1{b^2+1}+\frac1{c^2+1}\ge\frac34.$$
pumac-2012-finals-a-02.answer: Set $a=\tan A$, $b=\tan B$, $c=\tan C$ with $A+B+C=\pi$; the sum becomes $1-2\cos A\cos B\cos C\ge\frac34$ since $\cos A\cos B\cos C\le\frac18$.

pumac-2012-finals-a-03.prompt: Let $ABC$ be a triangle with incenter $I$, and let $D$ be the foot of the angle bisector from $A$ to $BC$. Let $\Gamma$ be the circumcircle of triangle $BIC$, and let $PQ$ be a chord of $\Gamma$ passing through $D$. Prove that $AD$ bisects $\angle PAQ$.
pumac-2012-finals-a-03.answer: The center $T$ of $\Gamma$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$ of the circumcircle of $ABC$ on line $AD$; power of the point $D$ shows $A,P,T,Q$ are concyclic and $TP=TQ$ gives the bisector.
